rv.q: Still, this is a first-hand, on-the-ground, observational theatre done with great wit.
The Bridge is a fast-paced, funny and captivating production that astutely connects the gap between warm comedy and sobering reality.
The Bridge is undoubtedly the call to action our theatrical landscape needs, and a powerful and assured one at that.
Shehada and Beale pull it off flawlessly, offering a show as gag-packed as any top-shelf comedy.

There’s also the improvised audience interactions, as the ‘bridge expert’ takes imaginary passports from those in the auditorium, and asks some audience members to hold the ropes tying down his luggage.

The Bridge is a production that demands to be seen, an absolute must in a world where both engaging with the oppression experienced around the world, and retaining our joy and hope for a better future are so, so important.
It's an evening that raises questions and has a point of view that comes across with power and passion.

They manage to find big, surprising laughs in the most absurdly frustrating bureaucratic hurdles, proving that comedy can be an incredibly potent weapon for survival and storytelling. It’s clever, poignant, and beautifully balanced. We are never just told what is happening, but rather shown with a wonderful clarity.

cn.t: Critics praise Shehada's charismatic performance in this autobiographical solo show, which skillfully balances sharp comedy with the tension and indignity of crossing from the West Bank into Jordan through Israeli checkpoints.
